programme.title: Na Trads
programme.desc: Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Alistair Heather leis a’ chuid as fheàrr bho Na Trads 2025 à Talla-ciùil Obar Dheathain. Le ceòl bho Mec Lir, Màiri NicAonghais, Rory Matheson Dance Band, Ellie Beaton agus Ross Miller Band am measg gu leòr eile, agus còmhradh le buannaichean is rionnagan an tachartais – an dà chuid air an àrd-ùrlar agus air cùl gnothaich. Mary Ann Kennedy and Alistair Heather present highlights from the 2025 Trad Awards from Aberdeen Music Hall. Featuring performances from Mec Lir, Mairi MacInnes, Rory Matheson Dance Band, Ellie Beaton and Ross Miller Band amongst others. Plus a catch-up with winners and stars both onstage and behind the scenes.

programme.title: Scottish Women's Premier League (BBC ALBA)
programme.desc: Join us for live SWPL action as top-of-the-table Rangers host current champions Hearts. With Micheal Steele and Clare Gemmell pitch-side from Broadwood Stadium. Thig còmhla rinn airson geama beò bho SWPL le Rangers a th’ aig mullach na lìg a’ cur failte air Hearts a bhuannaich an lìog an-uiridh. Tha a gheama slàn le Mìcheal Steele agus Clare Gemmell ag aithris bho stèideam Broadwood.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram sònraichte air DiDòmhnaich Cuimhneachaidh. Salm 124 air a sheinn le Ceòlraidh Ghàidhlig Ghlaschu, an laoidh Nam Aonar le Mo Smuaintinn le Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìleach Ghlaschu agus bidh An t-Urr. Aonghas Mac a' Ghobhainn ag innse mun àite a th' aig creideamh an lùib cogadh is call. Tha am prògram air aithris le Iain MacFhionghain. A special programme for Remembrance Sunday, with Psalm 124 sung by Glasgow Gaelic Choir and the hymn Nam Aonar le mo Smuaintinn by Glasgow Islay Gaelic Choir. Rev Angus Smith describes the part faith plays in war and loss. Presented by Iain MacKinnon.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets singer Mary Ann Kennedy in Ardgour. Although born in Glasgow, Mary Ann discusses how she has made her home in Ardgour and what that means to her. As they walk along Cona Glen, Mary Ann opens up about feeling comfortable in her own skin and how the environment has helped her find peace. She chats about her changing relationship with music and what brings her happiness. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri Màiri Anna NicUalraig ann an Àird Ghobhar. Ged a rugadh i ann an Glaschu, innsidh Mairi Anna an luach a tha i cuir air far a bheil i air a dachaigh a steidheachadh. A ’coiseachd tron Chona Ghleann, fuasglaidh Màiri Anna suas ma beachdan air a pearsa fhèin agus mar a tha an àrainneachd mu chuairt air a cuideachadh gus sìth a lorg. Tha conaltradh ann ma caochladh dhàimh le ceòl agus dè dìreach a tha toirt toileachas dhi. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Actress turned interior designer Erica Macpherson takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers, she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Nic a’ Phersain, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: Calum explores the underground sites of central Scotland. First, author Mairi Kidd introduces him to a lesser known history of Edinburgh below the city streets. Then he ventures under the busy platforms of Glasgow Central Station, where Calum discovers an atmospheric disused Victorian platform. In Dunoon, Calum gets help from his friend Kenny Rankin to access the Paper Caves and find out more about a story that dates back almost 350 years, connecting the Campbell clan with the site. ’S a’ phrògram mu dheireadh, nì Calum rannsachadh air làraich fon talamh ann am meadhan na h-Alba. Innsidh an t-ùghdair, Màiri Kidd, dha mun eachdraidh fo shràidean Dhùn Èideann air nach eil mòran eòlach. Fo àrd-ùrlairean trang Stèisean Rèile Meadhan Ghlaschu, gheibh Calum lorg air àrd-ùrlar iongantach, neo-chleachte bho linn Bhictòiria. Ann an Dùn Omhain, bheir a charaid, Coinneach MacFhraing, cuideachadh do Chalum gus Uamhan nam Pàipear a ruighinn agus tuilleadh ionnsachadh mu sgeulachd bhon t-seachdamh linn deug a tha a’ ceangal na Caimbeulaich ris an t-sreath uamhan seo. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke forage for nature’s bounty. Mary Ann heads to Northern Ireland to visit a good friend in County Down.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024 agus a’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Kathryn Tickell & The Darkening, Eòghann MacEunraig, Genticorum, TEUD & Kaïa Kater. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Kathryn Tickell & The Darkening, Ewen Henderson, Genticorum and intimate session recordings with TEUD & Kaïa Kater. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Rannsachadh air na dòighean annasach a tha fradharc bheathaichean air leasachadh. An exploration of the strange evolution of animal vision.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le The Island ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform The Island in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean ag ionnsachadh dè tha gabhail àite fon talamh – air leth inntinneach! Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are learning what happens underground - really interesting!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha a’ ghrian a’ deàrrsadh ‘s tha Ooona'son dhol a dh’iasgach. Tha May ag aontachadh cluich cuide ri Baba ach tha Baba a’ diùltadh faiche nan gràineag fhàgail gus an dùisg Spiky bho chadal-geamhraidh! It’s a beautiful day and Oona wants to practise fishing. May offers to play with Baba, who refuses to leave the hedghog burrow as he wants to wait until Spiky wakes from his hibernation!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona daonnan ann an cabhag ach tha Papa airson sealltainn dhi gum bi buthaidean a' gabhail cùisean air an socair. Saoil an tig aice air ionnsachadh rudan a dhèanamh ann an ‘Dòigh na Buthaide? Oona is forever in a hurry to learn and get things done, but Papa wants to show her that puffins tend to approach things in a slow and steady fashion. Will Oona master the ‘Way of the Puffin?’

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Nuair tha Fuigheag acrach a’ chiad char sa mhadainn, tha e feumach air biadh. Ach ciamar a gheibh e sin ‘s Boban na shuain chadail? When Fuigheag is hungry first thing in the morning, he needs food. But how will he get some with Boban fast asleep?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Le cuideachadh bho Burtaidh, tha Sif a’ toirt Pipp agus Bran air dàn-chuairt fèill spòrs. Ziff leads Pipp and Button on a fairground adventure with help from faithful Bertie.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Tha Sionnach airson ’s gum bi co-là-breith sònraichte aig Maigheach. Tha cuireadh aig Comhachag is Tosg, fhad ’s a bheir iad prèasant brèagha thuice, leithid dìthean le fàileadh cùbhraidh. Chan eil sin cho furasta ’s a shaoileas iad. Fhad ’s a tha iad trang a’ lorg nam prèasantan tha Maigheach air bhioran ’s I a’ feitheamh gus an tòisich am pàrtaidh co-là-breith aice. Fox wants to give Hare the best birthday ever. Owl and Tusk are invited, but only if they bring a nice present, like a beautifully scented flower. But that is not quite as easy as it seems. All the while Hare is kept waiting for her birthday party to start.

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Pompon 's a phàrantan ag ullachadh 'son turas air falbh, feumaidh Pompon tighinn gu co-dhùnadh air dè tha riatanach a thoirt leis sa bhaga aige. When Pompon and his parents prepare to go on a trip, Pompon must come to a decision as to what is essential for him to take in his bag.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ leughadh Famh agus Èirigh-na-grèine. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Jeanne Willis agus a dhealbhachadh le Sarah Fox-Davies. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Eilidh Cormack reads Famh agus Èirigh-na-grèine by Jeanne Willis, illustrated Sarah Fox-Davies and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.desc: Heat-loving hippies move into Mr Krabs' soup vat! Tha sgioba an tòir air blàths a’ lorg dachaigh anns a’ bhrot aig Mgr. Crùbag.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sgrudaire sgoile air nochdadh aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus chan eil Maighstir Mackle neo na tidsearan deiseil air a shon. Chan eil cùisean a’ coimhead ro mhath do Mhaighstir MhicFhraing ach tha Maighstir Strachan air a chasan, neo co-dhiù aona chois a lorg. Dè as urrainn a dhol ceàrr?! There’s a surprise visit from a school inspector at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. It’s not looking good for Mr MacFhraing, although Mr Strachan seems to have found his feet, well one foot at least. What could possibly go wrong?!

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Nuair tha Greta an cù a’ cèilidh air an sgoil, tha Flix airson a bhith taiceil dhi. Gu mì-fhortanach tha iad glè mhì-mhodhail nuair a tha ‘ad còmhla. Tha seo ag adhbharachadh trioblaid coin-cait ach the feum air fuasgladh cait-coin. When Greta the dog visits the school, Flix wants to be helpful to her. Unfortunately, they’re very badly behaved when together. This causes a dog-cat problem so what’s needed is a cat-dog solution!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Sona air a bhith trang a’ fàsgadh dhearcan ach tha e air cus den t-sùgh òl – tha sin ga fhàgail nas beòthail’ ‘s nas toilicht’ na bha e o chionn fhada. Abair gu bheil deagh ghumbladh a’ gabhail àit’! Sona has been busy pulping berries but he’s drunk too much of the juice - this has made him livelier and happier than he’s been for quite a while. There’s a lot of Gumbling taking place!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha an dithis mhealltair – Merri is Seonaidh – ri miastadh. Nuair a tha ’ad a' toirt seachad gheallaidhean nach meall ’ad na Gumbalan, tha ’ad a' tionndadh gus feuchainn ris a’ char a thoirt às na Bògaisean. Saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh? The two tricksters, Merri and Seonaidh, are up to no good. When they promise not to trick the Gumbals, they turn to playing mischief on the Bògaisean. How will they get on?

programme.title: Fillte
programme.desc: Fillte travels throughout Scotland, visiting the country’s finest woven craft producers. Tha Fillte a siuhbail fad Alba a lorg an obair-laimhne is fhearr, sa luchd-ciùird fighe a chruthaich e.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet Gaelic learner Caroline Quinn from Trinidad and Tobago, while Calum Maclean is in Portmahomack, Easter Ross, learning about his heritage.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Farpais-cheist do-chreidsinneach... Mas Fhìor! Le ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin, ’s iad an fheadhainn a chuireas na ceistean agus na freagairtean. An urrainn do Isla is Hamish agus Jamie is Liam a tha a’ cluich bhon stiùideo a’ chùis a dhèanamh orra airson an duais mhòr a bhuannachadh? A quiz show that is pretty unbelievable! Eight Pretenders play from the comfort of their own homes and hold all the questions and answers to this quiz. Can Isla and Hamish, or Jamie and Liam in the studio beat the Pretenders for a chance to win a cash prize? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill a’ bruidhinn ri clann a’ mhansa an là an-diugh. Cathy Macdonald talks to children of the manse.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: The arrival of potential Norwegian investor Johan throws a cat among the pigeons as age old family secrets and resentments come to the fore. The MacSween clan soon begin to realise that the mill is in worse shape than they thought and Seumas makes a surprise announcement to save the mill. Tha ruighinn, an neach-tasgaidh Nirribheach Johan a’ cur a' chiùil air feadh na fìdhle. Tha rùintean-dìomhair agus seann nàimhdeas an teaghlaich a’ togail ceann aon uair eile. Chan eil e a’ toirt fad sam bith mus tuig teaghlach MhicSuain gu bheil a’ mhuileann ann an staid fada nas miosa na bha iad an dùil agus tha a’ bheachd a th’ aig Seumas airson a’ mhuileann a shàbhaileadh a’ cur iongnadh orra uile. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc: Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus faighinn a-mach mun chrìoch eadar an Spàinn agus Moroco. Ann an Ceuta tha feansa àrd a’ sgaradh Afraga agus an Roinn Eòrpa agus dha mòran is e seo an geata chun na Roinn Eòrpa. Coinnichidh Ramsay ri imrichean a tha air a h-uile càil a tha aca a chuir ann an cunnart is iad a’ dol tarsainn air a’ bhalla an tòir air beatha nas fheàrr. Cluinnidh e bho luchd-còmhnaidh ionadail Ceuta a tha beò fo sgàil teannachadh poilitigeach agus coinnichidh e ri daoine a bhios ag obair gus an fheadhainn as motha a th’ ann an cunnart a chuideachadh. Ramsay MacMahon goes on a journey to find out about the border between Spain and Morocco. In Ceuta, a high fence separates Africa and Europe, and for many, this is the gateway to Europe. Ramsay meets migrants who have risked everything to cross the wall in the hope of a better life. He hears from local residents who live with the political tensions and meets people who work to help the most vulnerable. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le The Poozies le Wired to the Moon agus Sausage. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by The Poozies, featuring the tracks Wired to the Moon and Sausage. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: OMC!
programme.desc: Sketch show featuring a collection of comic characters and spoofs. Written by and starring the very best in emerging and established comic talent. Featuring Iain Beggs, Darren Maclean, Carina Macleod, Claire Frances MacNeil, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan and David Walker. Includes the latest updates from the ferry office, a recipe with a difference, and red hot passion finds physical expression via a clown love triangle. Anns an ceithreamh prògram bho shreath ùr OMC! chì sinn tuilleadh sgeidsichean loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail bho na sgriobhadariean is cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann. Gheibh sinn an turas sa beachd car eadar-dhealaichte airson reasabaidh, tha cridhe Doodles an cleasaiche a’ briseadh agus, ’s e cheist as motha an t-seachdan sa, am bidh an aiseig a’ seòladh? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha cuid dhe na rudan as fheàrr le Àtaidh agus Tilidh a dhìth. A bheil cuideigin air an goid? ’S e rùn-dìomhair a th’ ann! Some of Abney and Teal’s favourite objects are missing. Has there been a robbery? It’s a mystery!

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Stan and his friends are at the Ley to do a nature survey but strangely, there doesn't seem to be anything to spot. Where has all the wildlife gone? Tha Dan 's a charaidean aig an Loch gus suirbhidh nàdair a choileanadh, ach gu h-annasach, chan eil dad ann ri amharc. Ach càit' an deach am fiadh-bheatha?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Gilleasbaig Fearghasdan a’ leughadh Am Prionnsa Cinders. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Babette Cole agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. Gilleasbaig Ferguson reads Am Prionnsa Cinders, written and illustrated by Babette Cole and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha Hilda a’ tionndadh gu leabhar dìomhair airson ionnsachadh mar a chuidicheas i beathannan Dhaibhidh agus a màthair – ach, mo chreach, abair gu ‘eil a coibhneis cosgail is croiseil dhaibh uile. Hilda turns to a mysterious book to learn how she can better the lives of Daibhidh and her mother, but being kind proves to be costly and problematic for all.

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc: Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Fiach a’ tadhal orra? The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge, but who will emerge victorious as Fiach joins them?

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc: Àm partaidh – ‘s tha na Farpaisich làn plòigh agus gàirdeachais ach chan eil mi smaoineachadh gun còrd an onghail ris na nàbaidhean. Party time, and the competitors are full of fun and joyfulness, but I don’t think that the neighbours will approve of the noise.

programme.title: A-null ’s a-nall
programme.desc: Tha Isra cho toilichte nuair a tha i a’ faighinn an cothrom càmpadh mar a sìnnsearan - na Bedouin - còmhla ri a caraid, Laoise. Isra is delighted when she gets the chance to go camping like her ancestors, the Bedouin, with her friend, Laoise.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Tha na seòid a’ cnuasachadh air biadh a tha math sa gheamhradh agus a’ cruthachadh soithichean eadar-dhealaichte a bheir dhuinn blàths is cofhurtachd. Tha Ruairidh a’ deanamh Stiubha le Càl Dearg agus Feòil-Uain le Sabhsa Mionnt. Tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh Ròst Feòil-Chaorach le crumbail ubhal geamhraidh airson a ghabhail às a dhèidh. Gus crìoch a chur air a’ phrògram, tha Ruairidh ag ullachadh Teatnaidh Biotais agus tha Ùisdean a’ sealltainn dhuinn mar a ni sinn Uisge-beatha air a dhèanamh le smeuran. The lads contemplate winter and come up with a variety of heart-warming comfort foods. Ruairidh cooks red cabbage and a lamb hotpot with mint sauce. Uisdean prepares a mutton chump roast followed by a winter apple crumble. Ruairidh then prepares a beetroot chutney and Uisdean shows us how to make bramble whisky. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean is on the hunt for a world-famous dish which was created in an Indian restaurant in Glasgow.

programme.title: An Là

programme.title: Surfing: Marcachd an Tuinn/Riding the Wave
programme.desc: Tha Ceitlin Lilidh a’ toirt thugainn sreath de dhà phàirt air eachdraidh surfadh air feadh an t-saoghail. Ceitlin Lilidh's series on the world history of surfing.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill a’ bruidhinn ri clann a’ mhansa an là an-diugh. Cathy Macdonald talks to children of the manse.

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Cairistiona Cheannadach. Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee with guest Kristine Kennedy.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram sònraichte air DiDòmhnaich Cuimhneachaidh. Salm 124 air a sheinn le Ceòlraidh Ghàidhlig Ghlaschu, an laoidh Nam Aonar le Mo Smuaintinn le Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìleach Ghlaschu agus bidh An t-Urr. Aonghas Mac a' Ghobhainn ag innse mun àite a th' aig creideamh an lùib cogadh is call. Tha am prògram air aithris le Iain MacFhionghain. A special programme for Remembrance Sunday, with Psalm 124 sung by Glasgow Gaelic Choir and the hymn Nam Aonar le mo Smuaintinn by Glasgow Islay Gaelic Choir. Rev Angus Smith describes the part faith plays in war and loss. Presented by Iain MacKinnon.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Stan and his friends are at the Ley to do a nature survey but strangely, there doesn't seem to be anything to spot. Where has all the wildlife gone? Tha Dan 's a charaidean aig an Loch gus suirbhidh nàdair a choileanadh, ach gu h-annasach, chan eil dad ann ri amharc. Ach càit' an deach am fiadh-bheatha?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Le cuideachadh bho Burtaidh, tha Sif a’ toirt Pipp agus Bran air dàn-chuairt fèill spòrs. Ziff leads Pipp and Button on a fairground adventure with help from faithful Bertie.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ mì-thoilichte oir chan fhaod e cluich leis an spàin bhrot’ oir tha ro mhòr dha. Gu fortanach, tha Beag a’ moladh gum faod e taic a thoirt dhaibh-san le bhith toirt am brot air ais dhan uamh – is abair g’eil e taiceil! Baby Soup Dragon is unhappy - he isn’t allowed to play with the soup spoon as it’s too big for him. Fortunately, Small suggests that he can help to deliver the soup instead - and he is hugely helpful!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha bogsa dìomhaireachd air laighe air a’ phlanaid, le rudan annasach na bhroinn - clobhdan a tha nan tuill cuideachd. Tha e comasach dha na Clangairean siubhal tro na tuill seo - agus abair gu bheil iad trang a’ siubhal! A mysterious box has landed on the planet, with curious things inside it - cloths which are also holes. The Clangers can travel through these holes, and they do it a lot!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha tòrr spòrs aig Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur an ìre gur e ròbotan a th’ annta, gus am brùth cuideigin aca putan is tha an aileag a’ tòiseachadh air Peicein. Carson nach stad an aileag aige? Bheil smachd aig cuideigin air à àiteigin eile? Chan urrainn do Ghriogair sguir a shreothartaich, Lòra a mhèaranaich neo Raghnall a chasadaich. Saoil a bheil iad uile a’ tionndadh nan ròbotan dhà-rìribh? Petit and his friends are having a lot of fun pretending to be robots, until one of them presses a button and Petit gets the hiccups. Why can't he stop hiccupping? Is someone else controlling him from somewhere? Greg can't stop sneezing, Laura yawns and Roman coughs. Could it be that everyone is turning into real life robots?

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha an t-Iasg Ceann-chaorach gu math lìogach - tha fiaclan orra a dh’itheas cha mhòr rud sam bith agus tha iad math air biathadh nan iasgair a ghoid, gun duine greim fhaighinn orra. The Sheepshead Fish is very sneaky - they can eat pretty much anything as they have very sharp teeth and can steal the bait off fishing hooks, without getting caught.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mòrag Anna NicNèill a’ leughadh A’ Choinean Chòir. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Katie Cotton agus a dhealbhachadh le Blanca Gomez. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Morag Ann MacNeil reads A’ Choinean Chòir by Katie Cotton, illustrated by Blanca Gomez and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Bethany – An Dannsair Gaidhealach/The Highland Dancer
programme.desc: Young Bethany sets herself a daunting challenge - performing the notoriously difficult sword dance, at a major Highland dancing competition in Stornoway.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha Sebastian cho toilicht’ nuair a tha e a’ faighinn seann leabhar-latha beanntan Chaspair – leabhar air leth sònraicht’. Gu mì-fhortanach ge-tà, tha Mgr. Turner ga thoirt bhuaithe, mar pheanas. Ciamar a gheibh e air seo innnse do Chaspair? Sebastian is so happy when he gets Caspar’s old mountain journal, a very special book. Unfortunately, Mr Turner confiscates it as a punishment. How can he tell Caspar about this?

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo bheir i sùil air an neach-ealain ainmeil Hilma Af Klint agus seallaidh i dhut mar a nì thu dealbh anns an stoidhle aicese. Choirstaidh is back with another programme from her studio A’ Chùil. She takes a look at the famous artist Hilma Af Klint, and shows you how to make your own picture in her style.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha Bitzer air fois fhaighinn agus Seonaidh bochd fo gheasaibh aig Mowermouth an Gobhair. Ge-tà leis an treud air fad fo smachd Mowermouth, tha Bitzer a' tuigse gu bheil feum aige air a dheagh charaid. Bitzer gets his wish for some peace and quiet when Shaun becomes hypnotised by Mowermouth the goat and finally stops bothering him. But with the whole flock under the influence of Mowermouth's powerful gaze, Bitzer soon realises just how much he needs his old buddy.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Nuair tha Greta an cù a’ cèilidh air an sgoil, tha Flix airson a bhith taiceil dhi. Gu mì-fhortanach tha iad glè mhì-mhodhail nuair a tha ‘ad còmhla. Tha seo ag adhbharachadh trioblaid coin-cait ach the feum air fuasgladh cait-coin. When Greta the dog visits the school, Flix wants to be helpful to her. Unfortunately, they’re very badly behaved when together. This causes a dog-cat problem so what’s needed is a cat-dog solution!

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Tha na seòid a’ cnuasachadh air biadh a tha math sa gheamhradh agus a’ cruthachadh soithichean eadar-dhealaichte a bheir dhuinn blàths is cofhurtachd. Tha Ruairidh a’ deanamh Stiubha le Càl Dearg agus Feòil-Uain le Sabhsa Mionnt. Tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh Ròst Feòil-Chaorach le crumbail ubhal geamhraidh airson a ghabhail às a dhèidh. Gus crìoch a chur air a’ phrògram, tha Ruairidh ag ullachadh Teatnaidh Biotais agus tha Ùisdean a’ sealltainn dhuinn mar a ni sinn Uisge-beatha air a dhèanamh le smeuran. The lads contemplate winter and come up with a variety of heart-warming comfort foods. Ruairidh cooks red cabbage and a lamb hotpot with mint sauce. Uisdean prepares a mutton chump roast followed by a winter apple crumble. Ruairidh then prepares a beetroot chutney and Uisdean shows us how to make bramble whisky. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Claire Macleod from the Isle of Scalpay is Joy’s guest in the studio and Calum Maclean is on the hunt for some important pillars on the Isle of Skye.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets Kim Carnie on the island of Kerrera, where they walk along picturesque bays with panoramic views of Oban Bay and the Slate Islands. Kim discusses the importance of Gaelic in her life and how that has shaped her career as a singer. She opens up about love and identity, and how that has evolved over the years, whilst enjoying the surrounding nature and fresh autumn air. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay a’ coinneachadh ri Kim Carnie air eilean Chearrara far a bheil iad air an cuartachadh le bàghean àlainn agus seallaidhean air leth den Òban agus na h-Eileanan Sglèata. Innsidh Kim cho cudromach ‘s a tha Gàidhlig na beatha ‘s a bhuaidh a tha seo air a thoirt air a beatha agus air a dreuchd na seinneadair. Gu follaiseach dèidheil air àm an fhoghair agus an àrainneachd ghlan mun cuairt, tha i fuasgladh suas ma beachdan air gaol, fèin-aithne agus mar a tha sin air obrachadh a-mach na beatha fhèin. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc: Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus ionnsachadh mun sgaradh mòr eadar beartas agus bochdainn ann an São Paulo, Braisil. Bho na coimhearsnachdan beartach glaiste air cùl gheataichean tèarainteachd gu na favelas a tha a’ cuir thairis le sluagh, tha ballachan do-fhaicsinneach a’ sgaradh dhaoine bho chèile sa bhaile seo. Air an turas aige, cluinnidh Ramsay bho dhaoine a tha feuchainn ris an sgaradh seo a thoirt às a chèile le bhith a’ cruthachadh chothroman do dhaoine ann an cuid de na coimhearsnachdan far a bheil an ana-chothrom as motha ri fhaicinn. Ramsay MacMahon goes on a journey to find out about the deep divide between wealth and poverty in São Paulo, Brazil. From the affluent gated communities to the overcrowded favelas, invisible walls separate people in this city. On his journey, Ramsay hears from individuals who are determined to break down division by creating opportunities for people within some of the city's most disadvantaged communities. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Am buannaiche dhuaisean Calum McIlroy agus còmhlan-ciùil aig Duaisean nan Trads 2024. Anns an t-seata, Strathspeys & Reel, The Banks of Newfoundland agus Polonessa Spoof. Award-winning musician Calum McIlroy and band, recorded at the 2024 Trad Awards. The set includes Strathspeys & Reel, The Banks of Newfoundland and Polonessa Spoof.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. Le seann charaid na chuideachd, siubhailidh Coinneach MacFhraing a Shealtainn air tòir slighean ùra is dùbhlain bharraichte. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc: In the fire, Notre-Dame cathedral lost its light and soul - researchers are working to restore the many things that perished.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le Alive ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform Alive in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: The arrival of potential Norwegian investor Johan throws a cat among the pigeons as age old family secrets and resentments come to the fore. The MacSween clan soon begin to realise that the mill is in worse shape than they thought and Seumas makes a surprise announcement to save the mill. Tha ruighinn, an neach-tasgaidh Nirribheach Johan a’ cur a' chiùil air feadh na fìdhle. Tha rùintean-dìomhair agus seann nàimhdeas an teaghlaich a’ togail ceann aon uair eile. Chan eil e a’ toirt fad sam bith mus tuig teaghlach MhicSuain gu bheil a’ mhuileann ann an staid fada nas miosa na bha iad an dùil agus tha a’ bheachd a th’ aig Seumas airson a’ mhuileann a shàbhaileadh a’ cur iongnadh orra uile. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: The BBC's 2025 ghost story for Christmas, Mark Gatiss's adaptation of EF Benson's The Room in the Tower. It's 1944, and while sheltering during an air raid, Roger strikes up a conversation with Verity, a Wren. When he asks if she dreams, he begins to recount the haunting vision that has followed him for most of his life: a recurring dream of a mysterious house, a silent family on the lawn and an unseen, unidentified terror lurking in the room in the tower. But when he is invited to stay at a country estate eerily similar to the one in his dreams, and is assigned the very same room, he becomes increasingly disturbed as his nightmares begin to become reality. What is really waiting for him in the room in the tower?

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: In her final days, Edith Nesbit recounts the chilling tale of newlywed Victorians Jack and Laura. As they settle into a small cottage in a quiet village, they soon find their idyll overshadowed by the superstitious warnings of their housekeeper and the legend of two marble tomb effigies who are said to rise each year and walk. Jack dismisses this is as mere folklore. But as the fateful night draws near, he makes a terrifying discovery. And back at the cottage, Laura is all alone...

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: It’s 1881, and Old College, Oxford plays host to three very different academics. Abercrombie Smith is a model of Victorian manhood, clean of limb and sound of mind. Monkhouse Lee is a delicate and unworldly student from Thailand. And occupying the rooms between them is the strange and exotic Edward Bellingham, whose unnatural researches into the secrets of ancient Egypt are the talk of the college. Can Bellingham’s experiments truly bring the breath of life to the horrifying bag of bones that is the mysterious Lot No 249?

programme.title: Miss Marple
programme.desc: Miss Marple is convinced that the death of the schoolgirl Pamela Reeve holds the key to the mystery of the double murder. There are a number of suspects, but the police finally arrest Basil Blake. Miss Marple, however, draws an entirely different conclusion. After a train journey to London, she comes back with evidence that allows the police to stage a trap for the real killer.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: British Rail decides to close down the local station, and Audrey goes into battle.

programme.desc: A look at Pembrokeshire’s wild and rugged coast, where life is defined by the rhythm of the seasons and the power of the sea.

programme.title: Secret Knowledge
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley tells the story of Bolsover Castle in Derbyshire. Built in the early 17th century, it became the pleasure palace of playboy Cavalier and ambitious courtier William Cavendish. Guiding us on a tour of the castle and its remarkable collection of artworks, Lucy brings to life the spectacular masque held by Cavendish to win the favour of King Charles I. And from within the walls of this eccentric architectural gem emerges a colourful tale, capturing the tensions of early 17th-century England that would eventually lead the nation to civil war.

programme.title: War Grave
programme.desc: Intimate and moving stories of loss and remembrance are told by friends and relatives of those killed in some of the major conflicts of the 20th century, from the First World War to the Falklands.

programme.title: Playing the Dane
programme.desc: Stars of theatre, television and film, including Jeremy Brett, Steven Berkoff, Richard Briers, Christopher Plummer, Ian McKellen and Christopher Walken, describe the challenge of playing Shakespeare's Hamlet.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: In 1964, a young Steven Berkoff was cast in one of his earliest screen roles, as a junior player in Hamlet in Elsinore, a BBC co-production with Danish television. Shot in Denmark by director Philip Saville, it starred Christopher Plummer as Hamlet and Michael Caine, in his only Shakespeare role, as Horatio. Here, Berkoff shares his memories of the production and how he got involved, gives his verdict on how the film stands up today and describes - as only he can - the excitement and inspiration he felt from watching Plummer and Caine at work.

programme.title: Hamlet at Elsinore
programme.desc: 1964 production of Shakespeare's famous play. Filmed in Elsinore, Denmark.

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: Sweden, 1863. A country not much visited by Englishmen. An exception is the inquisitive Mr Wraxhall, whose innocent rummaging through the archives of the noble de la Gardie family takes a sinister turn. Wraxhall becomes fascinated by the long-dead founder of the dynasty, the fearsome Count Magnus, a tyrannical ruler who dabbled in alchemy and who once made a strange journey to the Holy Land on most unholy business. Despite the warnings of his hosts, Wraxhall is drawn ever deeper into the Count’s dark world and discovers that the dreaded aristocrat may not lie easy in his tomb...

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: 1923. Edward Williams, gentleman and amateur golfer, lives an untroubled life as the curator of a small university museum. His speciality is the topography of the British Isles. So when an art dealer sends him details of an interesting engraving - a mezzotint - of an old country house, he’s intrigued. When the picture arrives, however, it seems perfectly ordinary - until Williams notices a figure in the picture where there was none before. A cloaked figure, with a skull-like head and legs that are horribly thin. Soon, within the mezzotint, the figure seems to be on the move across the moonlit lawn towards the house with murderous intent. Long-forgotten secrets rise to the surface as Williams and his friends summon all the rational forces at their command to confront the impossible.

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: Adaptation of a ghost story by MR James. 1684. John Martin is on trial for his life. Facing him, the infamous 'hanging judge' George Jeffreys. However, this is not a cut-and-dried murder case.

programme.title: A Ghost Story for Christmas
programme.desc: Mark Gatiss brings the Christmas ghost story tradition back to life with The Dead Room, the tale of a long-running radio horror series of the same name. Simon Callow (Victoria & Abdul, Shakespeare in Love, Four Weddings and a Funeral) plays Aubrey Judd, the veteran presenter of the series and national treasure, who finds that he must adapt to changing times and tastes. But whatever happened to the classic ghost stories? The good old days?

And from within the walls of this eccentric architectural gem emerges a colourful tale, capturing the tensions of early 17th-century England that would eventually lead the nation to civil war.

programme.desc: Three-part series that looks at a year in Alaska, revealing the stories of pioneering Alaskans, both animal and human, as they battle the elements and reap the benefits of nature's seasonal gold rush.

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: The 18th century heralded the greatest blossoming of Scottish artistry in its history. The most powerful and influential figures in Britain clamoured to have their portraits painted by Allan Ramsey and Henry Raeburn, and their houses designed by Robert Adam. They stood in awe at the epic Highland landscapes of Horatio McCulloch and wept at the sensitive genre paintings of David Wilkie. Scots artist Lachlan Goudie explores how the intellectual revolution of the Enlightenment and the classical influence of the continent gave these artists the confidence and the inspiration to forge a whole new artistic landscape. From dusty storerooms of Edinburgh to the dazzling antiquities of ancient Rome, this is a journey of startling contrasts - between the past and the future, between the forces of reason and romance, between Presbyterian restraint and unfettered emotion. Out of the ashes of the Reformation, a new culture identity was beginning to emerge, and it was built on art.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Surrey University. The specialist subjects are venomous reptiles, the history of the Liberal Party since 1877, France in the 17th century and Tolkien's fiction.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson hosts the popular panel game of word definitions and deceptions. Team captains Frank Muir and Arthur Marshall are joined by guests Jane Lapotaire, Dr Robert Burchfield, Ruth Madoc and Melvyn Bragg.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team journey to La Palma, where giant new telescopes and cutting-edge science are opening extraordinary new windows to the universe.

programme.title: Joan Sutherland
programme.desc: Soprano Joan Sutherland talks to Bernard Levin and sings scenes from some of her most celebrated roles. With the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, led by Erich Gruenberg and conducted by Richard Bonynge.

programme.title: Metalworks!
programme.desc: Art historian and curator Tobias Capwell celebrates the great age of armour. Referencing the unstoppable rise of the Royal Almain Armoury at Greenwich, he tells the forgotten story of how Henry VIII fused German high technology with Renaissance artistry in the pursuit of one aim - to become the very image of the perfect knight. Using the talents of foreign craftsmen and his court artist Hans Holbein, Henry transformed himself into a living metal sculpture. His daughter Elizabeth I further exploited that image, making her courtiers parade before her in the most innovative and richly decorated works ever commissioned in steel.

programme.desc: Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke discover Barcelona through its art and architecture, including the frescoes that inspired Miro and a surprising collection of vintage fans.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Magnificent Monuments
programme.desc: Steeplejack Fred Dibnah considers the development of castles, from early Iron Age forts to secret underground tunnels used during the Second World War. At Hadrian's Wall, he marvels at the design of Roman toilets, while in Warwick, he joins a band of medieval knights to test the castle's defences.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: A journey through six centuries of warfare in the company of military historian Professor Richard Holmes. In 1415, Henry V won a remarkable victory against a French force that outnumbered him by five to one. Professor Holmes retraces Henry's route to Agincourt and finds a story of heroism and brutality.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Stately sitcom. A repair bill for Audrey's Rolls-Royce finally convinces her to revert to four-legged horsepower.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Sitcom. When Hyacinth hears that Emmet is rehearsing a musical, she is beside herself. Unfortunately sorting out Daddy's antics has to take priority.

programme.title: The Stuarts
programme.desc: Presented by Dr Clare Jackson of Cambridge University, this three-part series argues the Stuarts, more than any other, were Britain's defining royal family. We tend to take today's modern United Kingdom for granted, but there was nothing inevitable about its creation. During the 17th century, the Stuarts grappled with the chaos of three separate Kingdoms, multiple religions and civil war. Britain has not known a century like it and some of the questions this dynasty faced have not gone away. In the opening episode, Clare looks at James VI and I's attempts to unite Scotland and England under the umbrella of his crowns and persuade his subjects to feel more 'British'.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: Manhood follows Dallas businessman Bill Moore as he sets out to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox and bring these procedures into the mainstream, positioning male cosmetic surgery as a growing part of the aesthetics industry. The film follows several men, including a gay porn star and a father of five, as they both put their bodies on the line and undergo procedures in pursuit of physical transformation. Through intimate access to both the practitioners selling the dream and the men buying into it, the film traces the insecurities, trauma and societal pressures driving each of them, while raising uncomfortable questions about the ethics of an industry built on male self-doubt. Filmed over two years, with dark humour and unexpected tenderness, Manhood is a timely and revealing portrait of identity and self-image as cosmetic surgery among men continues to rise.

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: In the concluding episode of the series, Jim encounters ever larger cosmic structures to reveal the latest breakthroughs in our understanding of the universe. For example, there’s the heliosphere, a vast cloud of solar plasma that surrounds and protects the solar system. Its unique physics help us understand why life is possible. Larger still, Jim comes face to face with our galactic home the Milky Way, a monstrous structure sculpted by the gravitational forces of dark matter. Jim finds out from pioneering researcher Adrian Fabian about the black hole at its centre, whose strange behaviour includes emitting the lowest note that can be heard in the cosmos. At an even greater scale, Jim encounters huge structures such as the Laniakea Supercluster, of which the Milky Way is only a tiny part. Then there’s 'the giant arc', a collection of galaxies that account for more than three per cent of the observable universe. Jim learns from its discoverer, British PhD student Alexia Lopez, that this gargantuan structure is forcing scientists to reassess their theory of how the universe evolves and may overturn some of the most fundamental principles in physics.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team journey to La Palma, where giant new telescopes and cutting-edge science are opening extraordinary new windows to the universe.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Magnificent Monuments
programme.desc: Steeplejack Fred Dibnah considers the development of castles, from early Iron Age forts to secret underground tunnels used during the Second World War. At Hadrian's Wall, he marvels at the design of Roman toilets, while in Warwick, he joins a band of medieval knights to test the castle's defences.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: A journey through six centuries of warfare in the company of military historian Professor Richard Holmes. In 1415, Henry V won a remarkable victory against a French force that outnumbered him by five to one. Professor Holmes retraces Henry's route to Agincourt and finds a story of heroism and brutality.

programme.title: The Stuarts
programme.desc: Presented by Dr Clare Jackson of Cambridge University, this three-part series argues the Stuarts, more than any other, were Britain's defining royal family. We tend to take today's modern United Kingdom for granted, but there was nothing inevitable about its creation. During the 17th century, the Stuarts grappled with the chaos of three separate Kingdoms, multiple religions and civil war. Britain has not known a century like it and some of the questions this dynasty faced have not gone away. In the opening episode, Clare looks at James VI and I's attempts to unite Scotland and England under the umbrella of his crowns and persuade his subjects to feel more 'British'.

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: In the concluding episode of the series, Jim encounters ever larger cosmic structures to reveal the latest breakthroughs in our understanding of the universe. For example, there’s the heliosphere, a vast cloud of solar plasma that surrounds and protects the solar system. Its unique physics help us understand why life is possible. Larger still, Jim comes face to face with our galactic home the Milky Way, a monstrous structure sculpted by the gravitational forces of dark matter. Jim finds out from pioneering researcher Adrian Fabian about the black hole at its centre, whose strange behaviour includes emitting the lowest note that can be heard in the cosmos. At an even greater scale, Jim encounters huge structures such as the Laniakea Supercluster, of which the Milky Way is only a tiny part. Then there’s 'the giant arc', a collection of galaxies that account for more than three per cent of the observable universe. Jim learns from its discoverer, British PhD student Alexia Lopez, that this gargantuan structure is forcing scientists to reassess their theory of how the universe evolves and may overturn some of the most fundamental principles in physics.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Magnificent Monuments
programme.desc: Steeplejack Fred Dibnah visits Hampton Court Palace and Cragside, one of the first homes to have electric lighting. He also examines restoration work on a 15th-century manor house.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: Wellington's victory against Napoleon in 1815 ended the most powerful European empire since the Romans. Professor Holmes visits the farms and fields where history hung in the balance.

programme.title: My Garden of a Thousand Bees
programme.desc: Wildlife film-maker Martin Dohrn is bee obsessed. He has found over 60 species in his Bristol garden, from giant bumblebees to scissor bees the size of a mosquito, which he films with mind-blowing results. Dohrn can identify individual insects and forms a remarkable relationship with one leaf-cutter bee he follows through its entire life.

programme.title: Building Sights
programme.desc: Architect James Stirling examines the Katharine Stephen Room, a rare books library at Newnham College, Cambridge, built in 1981-1982 to the designs of Joanna van Heyningen and Birkin Haward.

programme.title: The Planets
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox reveals the history of Saturn, which began life as a strange world of rock and ice. In time, it transformed into a gas giant, ring-less and similar looking to its rival, Jupiter.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: One of Britain's most acclaimed and respected directors, Ken Loach, is the man behind award-winning films like The Wind that Shakes the Barley, Land and Freedom and I, Daniel Blake - but in terms of impact, his most important piece will for many always be the BBC's 1966 television drama Cathy Come Home. Written by Jeremy Sandford, produced by Tony Garnett and with Carol White in the titular role, Cathy's look at the plight of Britain's homeless left viewers shocked and forced the nation to confront an issue that until then had largely been ignored. Here, Ken looks back on the experiences of making the film, and shares his insights into the reactions it generated. Critics like Mary Whitehouse attacked him and the BBC for abandoning impartiality and brainwashing the public, while others applauded a groundbreaking and important piece of campaigning drama.

programme.title: The Wednesday Play
programme.desc: Landmark 1960s TV play about a young couple and their children who are cruelly overtaken by events which lead them into an unrelenting trap of debt, homelessness and poverty.

programme.title: In Conversation
programme.desc: Actor Cillian Murphy, who played the lead role in Ken Loach's Palme d'Or-winning film The Wind That Shakes the Barley, talks to the director at the BFI Southbank about a prolific career dedicated to documenting social and political injustice, the importance of artistic collaboration, the often-overlooked humour in Loach's films, and the impact working with Loach had on his own approach to acting.

programme.title: TechXplore
programme.desc: BBC Tech journalist Paul Carter travels to Japan to showcase some Japanese moonshot innovations and meet the people behind them. Travelling across regions east and west of Tokyo, he reveals how advanced technologies are tackling global challenges - and how these ideas are flowing around the world. Japan faces issues such as climate change, energy insecurity, natural disasters, and an ageing population in especially acute ways. Paul discovers that these pressures have made the country a proving ground for some bold, high-impact solutions. In Ibaraki, he visits the world's largest operational fusion facility, now serving as a testbed for Europe's next era of clean energy. In Chiba, he explores mental-health technologies designed to help people not only live longer, but happier lives. In Kyoto, Paul experiences disaster-response innovations designed to help protect communities from extreme weather. And in Tohoku, he meets a new generation of AI-powered robots designed to support life on Earth - and, ultimately, beyond.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, explores what the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency might look like, analyses how the political deadlock in Israel could be broken, and looks at the difficulties and opportunities that artificial intelligence presents to science.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Would you let AI walk around your home? We explore the growing race to put humanoid robots into our homes and workplaces. We examine Meta's reported robot project, the rise of Chinese robot manufacturers, the privacy risks of machines that can see, hear and map our lives and whether robots are becoming Big Tech's next multi-trillion-dollar bet. Meta has reportedly built a humanoid robot called Max and, if Mark Zuckerberg gets his way, this could be the next frontier for artificial intelligence. After years of AI living on our screens, Silicon Valley is now racing to give AI a body, one that can see, hear, move through the world and interact with people in real life. Could a humanoid robot really become as common as a smartphone? Would you trust one to help around the house, care for an elderly relative, or perform tasks at work? And as companies spend hundreds of billions of dollars on AI, are robots the breakthrough the industry has been waiting for, or another expensive gamble destined to disappoint?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Jonathan Head reports from Thailand, where recent flooding has highlighted the growing challenges facing Bangkok. As climate change brings rising seas and more extreme weather across South East Asia, we examine why the Thai capital is among the region's most vulnerable cities. Plus: BBC Eye investigates the shadow war being fought inside Russia, speaking to two Russian men who claim to have secretly worked for Ukraine's intelligence services. Through rare first-hand accounts, we explore a clandestine world of covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting military personnel and infrastructure far from the battlefield.

programme.title: Clive Myrie's African Adventure
programme.desc: Nigeria is known as the ‘giant of Africa’, and Clive heads to one of the continent's largest cities, Lagos. In a bustling downtown market, he gets a workout with a team who are getting the market goers fit, and he meets up with an organic chef in an open-air seafood market to pick up some fresh red snapper, shrimp and prawns. He also hits the studio with some talented young musicians and experiences the vibrancy of Nigerian art.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Can Africa hold on to more of the wealth its metals and minerals are creating? Amid the rise of electric cars, data centres and the ‘electrification of everything’, a growing number of countries across the continent are putting restrictions on their raw materials. The Democratic Republic of Congo, Ghana and Zimbabwe are amongst those want to keep more of the jobs and prosperity they bring at home, but what will it take to succeed? The CEO of the International Council on Mining and Metals, Rohitesh Dhawan, warns there could be a chilling effect on new investments if the rules keep changing. However the African Development Bank’s chief economist, Kevin Urama, says Africa needs the jobs for its young people and that could benefit the rest of the world too. Plus, Ben Thompson hears from the CEO of Hitachi Energy, Andreas Schierenbeck, about exactly where the demand for electricity is coming from.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: Food enthusiast and baker Briony May Williams travels the length of Italy to ask: are Italians too fussy about their food? The United Nations cultural body Unesco has recently given the country's entire cooking tradition special status - that's everything from pasta to pizza, mozzarella to tiramisu. But many Italians have strong opinions about how, when and what to eat, and some unwitting faux pas from visitors can send purists into a frenzy. Briony meets the innovators adding controversial ingredients to pizza and new flavours to ice cream, and the traditionalists who want to keep things exactly as they are.

programme.title: Africa: From Reparations to Action
programme.desc: African Heads of State have gathered at the annual Elevate Africa Presidential Roundtable in Accra, Ghana, to examine how the push for reparations for the transatlantic slave trade can move from recognition and resolutions to meaningful action. In a special Focus on Africa roundtable discussion hosted by Waihiga Mwaura, leaders explore the role of African governments, the African Union, Caribbean partners, and the wider international community in advancing reparative justice. The conversation also looks ahead, asking how Africa can engage its young people in shaping the reparations agenda, strengthen ties with the diaspora, encourage investment and return migration, and create opportunities that support the continent's future development. Bringing together questions of historical accountability and future prosperity, the discussion challenges leaders to move beyond declarations and chart a practical path towards reparative justice and sustainable development.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Protests across Europe led by youth movements have drawn attention to the role of social media in spreading information and misinformation. Largely led by gen-Z, these protests have included references to films like The Hunger Games and The Avengers, and featured people in costumes taking part in 'aura battles', while memes of the demonstrations are shared online. Researcher Dr Nayana Prakash considers how online platforms, viral videos and AI-generated content are now an inextricable part of protest movements. After Russian TV sent a camera crew to report on a Welsh independence march, BBC Monitoring's Russia specialist Francis Scarr examines how Russian state media is reporting on independence movements across the world, and what this coverage reveals about the Kremlin's portrayal of European instability and decline. Filmmakers Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes reflect on their documentary One in a Million, which follows a Syrian family over ten years as they rebuild their lives after fleeing Aleppo. Centred on Israa, first seen aged 11, the film traces her journey through adolescence, marriage and motherhood as she navigates life between two cultures.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.desc: Sophie Raworth and Petroc Trelawny present live coverage from London as HM the King leads the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph. His Majesty will be joined on Whitehall by senior members of the royal family and leading UK politicians, alongside representatives of the armed forces, the Commonwealth and faith communities for the two-minute silence at 11 o’clock and the National Service of Remembrance. This is followed by the annual wreath laying and the historic march past of 10,000 veterans as the nation remembers all those who have died serving their country. Accessible commentary and uninterrupted commentary-free coverage will be available on BBC iPlayer. A version with British Sign Language will also be available on Red Button and iPlayer.

Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and looks at if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. Justin asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

He decides to go for a complete, bold transformation, but finds himself completely out of his comfort zone in trying to hit both briefs.

programme.title: Designing the Hebrides
programme.desc: Banjo and his team are on South Uist in the Outer Hebrides. They’ve been called in to help crofters DJ and Lindsay, whose family have lived and worked the land there for generations. The couple want to turn their garage into a shop to sell their produce from. The dull breezeblock building has no character or charm, so Banjo has to work from scratch to transform this empty space. He searches for salvage around the island and from DJ’s crofter mum, and he decides to clad the walls in disused corrugated iron panels he finds around the island. But with a budget of only £4,000, will he pull off his homestead kitchen design vision?

programme.desc: It’s a glorious summer in Fife, and one of the park’s longest-serving staff, Billy, is preparing for a unique challenge - a skydive to mark his 80th birthday. programme.title: Scotland’s Sacred Islands with Ben Fogle
programme.desc: Arriving on the Isle of Barra, Ben discovers how his own hand-knitted Gansey fisherman’s jumper is inspired by the hazardous life on these islands. We find Ben aboard a fishing boat in a wild sea, heading for the remote and deserted Mingulay – the Isle of Whispering Ghosts. He learns how the extremes of life here forced the community to abandon it. Travelling across a causeway, Ben reaches South Uist and joins Paul McCallum - the Singing Crofter, who composes Gaelic hymns, singing them as he works. He believes that faith, work and song all go together. Journeying north, Ben finds the island’s iconic 30ft Our Lady of the Isles statue, which overlooks a Nato missile base to remind the military that a greater power watches them. Prince Charles came to the Hebrides for a week in 1987 to escape media scrutiny. No-one leaked his presence to the press, and Ben drops in for morning tea with the prince’s host, 90-year-old Gloria MacKillop, to learn the art of keeping a secret. Ben then camps down for the night on Hosta Beach to reflect on this stage of his pilgrimage and what he has gained from it.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Paramedics in Perth respond to a 999 call for Emily, a 13-year-old who has been injured during rugby practice at school, suffering a suspected broken arm and dislocated shoulder. The team now face the delicate and potentially dangerous task of moving her to the ambulance. Meanwhile, at the Inverness Ambulance Control Centre, Jackie organises help for a young teenager who is unresponsive after drinking eight cans of lager and a bottle of vodka, while Chloe speaks to a distressed bystander who has witnessed a severe motorcycle accident. Paramedic Stephen is part of the ambulance team on board the King Air. The team respond to incidents spanning the length and breadth of the country, and today he is helping to transport a patient from the island community of Stornoway to the specialist cardiac unit at Glasgow’s Golden Jubilee Hospital. In Glasgow’s Southside, David and Chanda have their first shift together as they treat an elderly cancer patient who is suffering from a possible infection. They also respond to a concerning call from a woman who has reported heavy bleeding and then abruptly hung up without leaving a full address.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: On the Isle of Skye, fairy tales are more than just stories. From magical pools promising eternal youth, to ancient bridges said to connect our world with the supernatural, the island’s fairy folklore draws thousands of curious visitors every year. But is it all a clever tourist trap, or does something deeper lie behind the legends? In this enchanting adventure, sceptic Zara joins folklore enthusiast Evelyn to investigate the mysteries of Skye’s fairy tradition. At the heart of their journey is Dunvegan Castle’s legendary Fairy Flag, an ancient relic said to have been gifted by a fairy and to hold the power to protect the MacLeod clan in battle. As they uncover dramatic tales of clan warfare, explore Gaelic songs and hear extraordinary stories passed down through generations, Evelyn and Zara discover a tradition woven into the island’s history, identity and culture. Could there be more to the fairies of Skye than meets the eye? And will the promise of eternal youth finally tempt Zara to believe in a little magic?

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Was Mary Queen of Scots responsible for her husband’s murder, or was she the victim of a ruthless plot to destroy her? Evelyn and Zara embark on a royal murder mystery to uncover the truth behind one of Scotland’s most infamous queens. From the shocking death of Lord Darnley to the mysterious Casket Letters, they follow a trail of scandal, suspicion and political intrigue, meeting historians who reveal the secrets behind the story. With affairs, betrayal and power-hungry nobles at every turn, the evidence raises serious questions about who really wanted Darnley dead. Was Mary a murderer, or was she framed by those determined to control her? As her story unfolds, a woman’s fight for power becomes a battle for her reputation, and the legacy she left behind.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.desc: Mid Wales is today's destination on Christine Walkden's balloon tour of some of Britain's finest gardens. At Powis Castle Garden, she learns how to brace an ancient yew and meets David, whose family had worked there for generations. At the Dingle Garden, she helps to restore an obscured view. We also hear the story of Mona Holloway, a wartime land girl who found love on a neighbouring farm.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: At Forest Green Rovers, known as the ‘little club on the hill’, Vick Hope discovers how a team from a small Gloucestershire hamlet made it into the professional leagues, before trying her hand at mowing the pitch with the club’s groundsman. Matt Baker follows the journey of a locally brewed organic beer from barley field to pint glass and meets the greengrocer supplying fresh produce to the world’s first fully vegan football club. He then heads into the kitchen to see how that seasonal veg ends up on the players’ plates. Meanwhile, Adam Henson is on the lookout for two new signings of his own as he heads to Yorkshire to find some fresh recruits for his white park herd back in Gloucestershire.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads to the annual autumn calf sale in the historic Newton Stewart mart and finds out how this special building is still going strong over a century after it was built. Cammy is in Dumfries and Galloway, where he examines what the arrival of the bluetongue virus means for Scottish farmers and hears from the chief vet. Shahbaz is on the Morvern Peninsula, where she heads underground to explore Europe’s only silica sand mine. Ahead of Children in Need, Arlene is in the Borders, where she visits a charity near Selkirk that uses the healing power of horses. And Leanna is in North Sutherland finding out about community efforts to save the endangered great yellow bumblebee.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek is hunting down his most terrific treks from the south. His first quest is an adventure between two captivating castles - Caerphilly and Castell Coch, where he gets the chance to don a full suit of armour. Next, Derek is in Gower walking from Fall Bay to Oxwich, where he discovers a mysterious clifftop hideaway and learns how this area used to be a haven for smugglers. On the way, he tries abseiling, cold-water swimming and foraging for seaweed. The last walk Derek remembers is in the wonderful Wye valley, where he marvels at one of the UK’s first tourist walks, takes to the water in a canoe and visits the awe-inspiring Tintern Abbey, where he witnesses the relics of a remarkable archaeological excavation.

programme.title: Swallows and Amazons (2016)
programme.desc: Four children dream of escaping the tedium of a summer holiday with their mother. When finally given permission to camp on their own on an island in the middle of a vast lake in the Lake District, they are overjoyed. But when they get there, they discover they may not be alone. The battle for ownership of a lonely island teaches them the skills of survival, the value of friendship and the importance of holding your nerve. Based on the novel by Arthur Ransome.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: For a live demonstration of terroir, Eva heads to Domaine Dujac, home of the current most-wanted Burgundy wine. Standing on one side of a road, owner Jeremy Seysses points to a parcel of grand cru (the very best) of Clos de la Roche. On the other side is a premier cru (the next best) - a Gevrey-Chambertin Combottes. Back at the winery, Eva tucks into beef cheeks bathed in Domaine Dujac for a classic boeuf bourguignon lunch. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles presents from Kingston in Surrey, with the reds and the blues led by experts Thomas Forrester and Gary Pe. Both teams are eager to make a profit at the auction, but who will win? While the competition hots up, Eric gets on his bike at the Herne Hill Velodrome.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Tommy is by the seaside in the Norfolk village of Eccles-on-Sea to see a very unusual wooden property that he fears may be beyond salvation. He’s also in Islington, north London, living the high life at a two-bed flat situated on one of the upper floors of a high-rise building. Dion is in Sheffield to view an intriguing auction lot comprising three terraced houses.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Live coverage of the FA Cup First Round tie between Cray Wanderers of the Isthmian League and League One Stockport County. Recognised as London’s oldest football club - pre-dating the FA Cup itself - seventh-tier Cray are making their maiden appearance in the 1st Round. Alex Scott presents from Flamingo Park in Chislehurst.

programme.title: The FA Cup
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad presents highlights from the first round of the FA Cup. London’s oldest club Cray Wanderers host Stockport County, who are flying high in League One, and non-league Stafford Rangers play Grimsby Town. 2021 FA Cup winners Leicester City travel to 6th tier Oxford City. Plus a full round-up of the weekend’s cup action.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Crystal Palace Park in south east London, where highlights include a diamond ring found wrapped up in a sock, a Louis Vuitton trunk and a surprise visit from a living artist. Will Farmer is delighted to see a pair of majolica whippets, while Jon Baddeley is stunned to discover a rare sundial by Thomas Tuttell that dates back to the end of the 17th century. Lee Young is intrigued by a trio of bronze Chinese censers bought from a flea market, while Ronnie Archer Morgan discovers clothing and correspondence with a direct link to Ethiopian ruler Haile Selassie. Fiona Bruce meets cartoonist Ralph Steadman, best known for his work with maverick American journalist Dr Hunter S Thompson, while Mark Smith challenges Fiona to identify secret Second World War spy gadgets concealed in everyday items. Clare Tole-Moir is thrilled to see a rare DIY kit dress by fashion designer Paco Rabanne, while John Foster admires a jointed wooden artist’s model with a surprising value.

programme.title: Remembrance Sunday: The Cenotaph
programme.desc: Highlights from the Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson visits a small village in Northumberland to find out how the family and village who both share the name Craster have had their lives and fortunes intertwined for over 800 years. The village sits on a unique seam of rock called the Whin Sill and next to the North Sea. Ben learns how, through the generations, the Crasters have used local resources to make their fortunes and in turn have changed the face and the fortunes of the village and the villagers. Ben meets Michael Craster, who still lives in the family’s 850-year-old tower and is an expert on his ancestors. Ben follows the family tree and hears of various heads of the family, such as the Georgian period’s Daniel Craster who developed quarrying in the village.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture to the northernmost reaches of the UK – Shetland – to fish the lochs and the seas of this remote and beautiful place for trout and pollock. Shetland is an archipelago of about 100 islands off the north east coast of Scotland, only around 15 of which are inhabited. It feels like they have entered a very different world - and it's full of surprises for both of them.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: After a hair-raising drive across the Conor Pass and a spot of seaside silliness hitting golf balls into the ocean, Bill bids farewell to Chris O'Dowd. In County Clare, Bill and Tom's attempt to sneak unnoticed into a hurling match goes awry, before an emotional reunion recalls an unforgettable act of kindness. Then, a chance invitation in Ballybunion leads to a freezing Atlantic challenge.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Is the ‘politics of nastiness’ over following the Democrats sweeping the House and Senate in the US midterms, and what does it mean for the tone of politics in the UK and Europe? Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Liverpool, discussing immigration, the US midterms, the costs on small businesses and slavery reparations. On the panel: deputy leader of the Labour party Lucy Powell, Conservative Luke Evans, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress Paul Nowak, columnist and commentator at the Telegraph Tim Stanley and psychologist and ex-NBA star John Amaechi/

programme.title: This City Is Ours

In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

From battling with the elements on the tip of Sutherland to a subtropical garden paradise in the Borders and growing with no soil, across the bridge over the Atlantic on the Island of Seil - these gardeners are all working on the very edges of Scotland.

programme.title: The Wooden Horse
programme.desc: Dramatisation of one of the most ingenious escape bids of World War II. In camp Stalag Luft III, the Nazis have built the prisoners' huts so far from the fence that underground escape is virtually impossible. One British officer, inspired by the tale of the Trojan Horse, proposes a daring plan to start a tunnel close to the boundary using a wooden vaulting horse as cover.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Normanby Hall, where finds include a marble bust gifted by a generous neighbour, valued at £15,000, and a pair of rare candlesticks won in a newspaper competition.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today, Flog It! comes from Dover Castle in Kent. Antique experts Catherine Southon and Jonathan Pratt search for items to take off to auction. Catherine falls for a colourful brooch and Jonathan unearths a horn beaker used by Winston Churchill. Paul Martin uncovers the story of Dover Castle’s secret tunnels.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor kicks off a new week by chatting exclusively to the latest couple to be eliminated from the competition. Also, Friday’s all-star Panel return for a deep dive into the weekend’s action.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Akisa Wandera reports from Angola, where billions of dollars are being poured into a vast new trade corridor at the centre of a global race for critical minerals. We examine what's at stake for the people living on the frontline of this transformation. Plus: BBC Brasil travels to the city of Camaçari, where Chinese carmaker BYD has opened its biggest factory in Latin America. As Chinese investment reshapes jobs, industry and daily life, we explore how one Brazilian city has become a test case for the growing rivalry between China and the United States.
